overview_markdown:
Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source, self-improving AI agent built around a closed learning loop: it autonomously creates skills after complex tasks, refines them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, and searches its own past conversations via FTS5 with LLM summarization. It pairs this with Honcho dialectic user modeling to build a deepening profile of each user across sessions, and it is compatible with the agentskills.io open standard.

Architecturally it is a Python application with a full terminal UI (multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, streaming tool output) plus a single gateway process that bridges Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and Signal with cross-platform conversation continuity. It is model-agnostic — Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, or custom endpoints — switchable at runtime with `hermes model`, and it ships an explicit `hermes claw migrate` command for OpenClaw users. Recent commits show heavy investment in token accounting (provider-calibrated image token costs), cache-write observability, plugin hook ownership, and CI public-surface diffing, indicating a mature, actively hardened codebase.

Compared to OpenClaw, Hermes differentiates on memory and self-improvement rather than raw action breadth: its skill-learning loop and cross-session recall are the headline features, while OpenClaw retains a larger overall community and footprint. Trade-offs include a heavier Python runtime, potentially high token spend on long agentic loops (a recurring Reddit complaint), and less documented sandboxing for tool execution.
